source.title: Probabilistic decision making by slow reverberation in cortical circuits

confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily replicated biophysical model that is the direct theoretical ancestor of the mechanism MECH-450 proposes: recurrent excitation plus feedback inhibition produces attractor settling that amplifies the difference between conflicting inputs and yields a categorical (winner-take-all) choice, rather than a one-shot global comparison. Mapping fidelity is high for the core 'settling competition replaces feedforward readout' assertion; the main transfer caveat is that the model is a two-/few-alternative cortical reverberation network, not the within-eligible _modulatory_accum field over a discrete action set, and it does not itself demonstrate that a strong modulatory channel can FLIP an F-dominated winner.
failure_signatures: If recurrent excitation / feedback inhibition is too weak, the network fails to reach a single high-activity attractor and the choice is not amplified to a categorical winner -- the indecision / blend-output pole MECH-450 predicts for too-few/too-weak settling rounds.

The amplification is driven by slow NMDA-mediated reverberation; with a fixed (unlearned) inhibition kernel and only a few settling rounds, the V3-bounded version may not have enough effective gain to override a large feedforward score gap.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A biophysically realistic cortical network with slow recurrent excitation and feedback inhibition produces attractor dynamics that amplify the difference between conflicting inputs and generate a binary categorical choice, reproducing decision-correlated firing, psychometric functions, and reaction times.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-450's core premise -- that a bounded recurrent settling competition (mutual/surround inhibition over the eligible set) can convert an additive _modulatory_accum BLEND into a competitive winner-take-most, rather than the one-shot argmin/softmax readout -- is the discrete-action, V3-bounded instance of exactly this cortical attractor mechanism.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Wang's network arbitrates between 2 (or few) competing populations driven by external sensory evidence; it does not model an F-dominated score field nor demonstrate that a strong non-dominant channel can flip the selected attractor away from the feedforward maximum. The claim's distinctive prediction (attractor FLIP) is plausible under this dynamics but is not directly tested here.
mapping.source_context: Computational/biophysical simulation of macaque area-LIP-style perceptual decision making (random-dot motion discrimination); spiking + reduced mean-field analysis.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational, highly cited, repeatedly validated model (source_quality very high). Mapping_fidelity high for the settling-vs-feedforward contrast but discounted because the FLIP claim and the discrete-eligible-set framing are not directly instantiated. Transfer risk moderate: cortical 2-choice reverberation -> discrete within-eligible BG-style competition is a real but well-precedented analogy.
